surfaces.coverage: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 48.22 km effective diameter (catalog ±0.6 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative. The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Ďurech2020 TableA.1 reports401 cyan plus174 orange ATLAS observations and two poles. Sparse photometry constrains broad convex shape; fine relief and a unique pole are unsupported.

surfaceSampling.previewPolicy: Radial rays with more than one distinct source intersection are withheld; the triangle atlas samples the source surface in 3D.

transfer.method: Closest full-source triangle point in 3D; source barycentric radius and normal. No radial branch selection.
